sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Sector 18?

items.d: We use individual protocol of stimulation for woman with less than 1.1 ng/ml AMH by using DuoStim technique along with micro dose flare.
In case of severe male factor such as low sperm count (oligospermia) with OATS or increased sperm DFI (>25%) and azoospermia (PESA/TESA/micro TESE).
If you have undergone unsuccessful IVF cycle in another hospital, 3D SIS and hysteroscopy will be performed. ERA can be performed in case of repeated failure.
We recommend doing embryo cryopreservation or banking. After 2 to 3 months of depo inj. do frozen embryo transfer.
Antagonist protocol is used and we trigger with agonist giving you no chance of OHSS.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: Tests required prior to starting IVF.
points: Check ovarian reserve: AMH levels and USG done on day 2 or 3 for good AFC.
Male workup: Semen analysis with CASA and halo sperm test should be done after 2 to 3 days abstinence.
Saline sonography: Performed to assess uterus receptivity. Biopsy of endometrium can be taken to check CD138.
Blood work: Thyroid profile and fasting insulin/HbA1C. Hormonal assessment of day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
Serology test for ART: Partner should do their HIV 1/2, HBsAg, Anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Your medical record will be evaluated. USG is done for follicle size and your past investigation will be reviewed.

steps.t: Protocol of Stim Will Run from Day 2 to Day 11 of Cycle
sub: From day 2 you will be started on injection given daily and monitored by USG and anti-Mullerian hormone.

steps.t: Pick Up of Eggs and Semen Analysis
sub: Procedure is carried out under local anaesthesia which takes approximately 15 minutes, USG guided. Sperm is processed in laminar flow.

steps.t: On Day 1 ICSI and 5th Day Embryo
sub: After ICSI is performed we will monitor embryo till day 5 to 6 which is called blastocyst.
Fresh or frozen embryo will be transferred under USG guidance using soft catheter.

sections.eyebrow: Investigations Required Before You Start IVF
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Test for female infertility: Hormonal levels are checked on day 2/3 of your period. We will test for ovarian reserve i.e. AMH and do a scan to calculate your Antral Follicle Count (AFC).
Semen analysis: For males we do a basic semen analysis. We recommend doing a CASA analysis. If needed we can also perform sperm DNA fragmentation.

sections.eyebrow: Steps We Perform During Your IVF Journey
sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

steps.t: Reviewing All Your Previous Workup and Response
sub: After looking at all your past ovarian response we design your protocol. And choose your medications as per your semen analysis.
Patient will be started on injectables on Day 2 of her cycle. She will undergo scans to see how she is responding to her medications. Usually lasts 8-11 days.

Your egg retrieval will be done on the day of procedure. It's a short procedure which takes around 15-20 min. Under local anaesthesia you will receive sedation to keep you relaxed. Your partner's sample will also be collected on the same day.
Eggs will be fertilized in lab by a process called ICSI. This means injecting one sperm inside an egg. These will be cultured for 5 days and blasts will be achieved if any.
On day 5 if we have blastocysts they will be transferred into your womb. Using USG as guidance we transfer the embryo. You will be prescribed to take medication post transfer.

items.d: Treatment with personalized stimulation DuoStim and mild stimulation + embryo cryopreservation.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Ovary testing: Blood test for serum AMH + TVS scan on day 2/3 to check how many follicles you have (ovarian reserve).
Sperm test: Computerized semen analysis + if report is abnormal do a DFI test.
Uterus cavity evaluation: Perform a 3D USG or SIS. Hysteroscopy if required.

Blood test for thyroid and prolactin: On day 2 of cycle test your TSH and prolactin levels. Other basic blood tests such as sugar (HbA1c) levels should also be checked along with basal hormone levels i.e. Day 2 FSH/LH and estradiol.
Screening for infections (mandated as per ART Act): Screen both partners for infections. HIV-I & II, Hep B (HBsAg), Hep C and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Review your past history and decide on how to stimulate your ovaries.
Start on medicines tailored for you and check your follicle growth via scan and hormone test on every alternate day.
A minor surgical procedure is performed to collect your eggs under mild anaesthesia. Your partner's sperm will also be collected at the same time.
Your eggs will be injected with your partner's sperm using ICSI. Embryos will be grown for 5 days (blastocyst).
The best embryo/s available will be transferred to you. After suitable lining preparation embryo will be transferred (fresh/frozen) and you will be put on medications.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Tests for your reserve (AMH & ultrasound).
Your partner's sperm analysis. DFI can be done if required.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: We will choose a protocol based on your age and AMH level, depending upon your male factor as well if present.
You will be provided injections for around 10–12 days, which we will monitor through scans and bloods.

On the day of your egg retrieval we will extract eggs from you. It's a day care procedure where the patient is given mild anaesthesia. Semen will be collected from your partner and sent to lab on the same day.
Your eggs will be put in the incubator for 5 days.

We will transfer your best embryo into your uterus as guided by USG, based on your embryology report. You will be provided medicines to help your uterine lining accept the embryo until you receive a positive result.

items.t: Looking to postpone childbearing or have low AMH levels
items.d: Protocols for patients in their late 30s or beyond are modified. Using either DuoStim or mild stimulation, we create an individualised stimulation protocol for you.
We offer egg freezing and an [embryo bank](/embryo-cryopreservation/).
If you have high DFI, consider the [Sperm DNA Fragmentation (DFI) test](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/). We can treat you accordingly. You might need ICSI as well.
Consider a freeze-all cycle and plan a [Frozen Embryo Transfer (FET)](/frozen-embryo-transfer/).
Individualised protocol using antagonist and agonist triggers, so you do not run the risk of OHSS.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Ovarian reserve test: AMH and TVS for counting AFC on Day 2/3.
Semen analysis with CASA and DNA Fragmentation Index.
Ultrasound (sonogram) or hystero-sonogram to check for any pathology in the uterus. Hysteroscopy can be performed if needed.
Hormonal profile: thyroid, prolactin and HbA1c, plus blood for Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
Mandatory investigations under the ART Act (husband and wife): bloods for HIV I and II, HBsAg and anti-HCV, along with VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

steps.t: Review of test results & protocol scheduling
sub: Your protocol is decided based on your ovarian reserve, cycles and your husband's semen report.
Injections are administered from Day 2 to Day 11, with TVS and blood tests to check your hormones.
Once your follicles are mature, eggs are collected on the puncture table under ultrasound guidance. Your husband's sample is received at our lab at the same time.
After egg collection we perform ICSI and raise the embryos in the incubator to Day 5.

steps.t: Blastocyst transfer on Day 5 (fresh or frozen)
sub: Under ultrasound guidance we place the blastocyst in your uterus, and you are given medicines after the transfer.

sections.eyebrow: What Tests Will Be Performed Before Your IVF/ICSI Procedure
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Test to evaluate ovarian function: blood test for AMH levels and a scan to find the number of eggs present in the ovary (antral follicle count) on Day 2 or 3 of your cycle.

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Kaushambi?

items.d: When fallopian tubes are blocked, it is good to find out if the blockage is partial or complete and then decide if you want to undergo surgery or move to IVF. Know more about [fallopian tube blockage](/fallopian-tube-blockage-treatment/).
If you have a past pelvic infection, you may require assessment for tubal damage or hydrosalpinx. This can be assessed prior to doing IUI or IVF.
Oligoasthenozoospermia can occur due to many causes. It is best to identify the root cause before moving towards IUI, IVF or ICSI. More info on [low sperm count](/low-sperm-count-oligospermia/).

When there is no sperm in the semen sample, it is essential to know the cause. We can perform blood tests and a scrotal Doppler and determine if sperm can be obtained from the testes. Read more on [azoospermia](/azoospermia-treatment/).
Polyps, adhesions / Asherman's syndrome or septums can all be identified and corrected by performing a hysteroscopy. This is done as a daycare procedure.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
sections.oneline: A few tests that we might want you to do prior to starting IVF. Depending upon your condition more or fewer tests may be done.
points: Day 2 blood AMH level and transvaginal ultrasound to assess the number of antral follicles.
Day 2 semen sample. If needed, we will do a DNA fragmentation index test.
Day 2 ultrasound: we will perform a 3D scan / saline infusion sonography to see if there is any uterine abnormality. In some instances we will perform a hysteroscopy.
Other blood work: TSH, prolactin levels and HbA1c. On day 2 we will also collect blood for baseline hormones.
Tests on partner: we will need some blood work on both male and female for infective agents like HIV, hepatitis B, C and syphilis.

sections.eyebrow: What Will My Protocol Look Like?
sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: We will review your past medical history and previous treatment. This will include checking your ovarian reserve and semen report if needed. Based on this we will decide your protocol.

Between Day 2 and 11 we will begin stimulation of your ovaries with injections. You will have to come to the clinic every couple of days for a scan to see how your ovaries are responding, along with blood hormone levels.

Around Day 11–12 your eggs will be mature and ready for collection. This is done with a simple procedure under sedation. It will take less than 45 minutes and you will be discharged from our clinic the same day. Your partner will be asked to provide a sample, which will be processed in our lab.
Sperm and egg will be combined in our lab by the process called ICSI. The embryo will be cultured for 5 days. We keep our embryos in an incubator until we have healthy embryos to transfer.

Embryo transfer will be done on Day 6 after embryo culture. One or more blastocysts will be selected and placed inside your uterus under a scan. Luteal support medicines will be started after transfer.

items.d: Blocked fallopian tubes need assessment and then tubal repair or IVF. Learn more about [fallopian tube blockage](/fallopian-tube-blockage-treatment/).
Pelvic infection causes scarring of the tubes, which may require assessment (and treatment) before attempting IVF.

Polyps, adhesions or septums within the uterus can be diagnosed and treated hysteroscopically.

sections.eyebrow: Exactly What Happens Before You Start IVF Treatment?
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
sections.oneline: Before starting your IVF treatment we sit down with you to review all your past fertility test results. We believe there is no need to run every test before beginning IVF. The key tests are ovarian reserve testing and semen analysis. By knowing your ovarian reserve we can personalise your IVF medications.
points: Ovarian reserve testing: serum AMH and a Day 2/3 transvaginal scan for antral follicle count (AFC).
Semen assessment: computer-assisted semen analysis (CASA) with DNA fragmentation testing when indicated.
Uterine cavity screening: 3D sonography or saline infusion sonography, with hysteroscopy when needed.
Hormone and metabolic profile: TSH, prolactin, HbA1c and baseline Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
ART Act serology for both partners: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Testing and review of previous fertility treatments along with your ovarian reserve test and semen analysis results allows Dr Mona to personalise your medication protocol.
All our gonadotropin doses are tailor-made for you and tracked with ultrasound scans of developing follicles. Hormone levels are also monitored at this stage.
Egg collection day involves small procedures for both you and your husband. While your eggs are being collected, your husband's sperm is prepared in the laboratory.
Fertilisation can be done using IVF or ICSI. We usually grow your embryos to the blastocyst stage prior to embryo transfer.
We perform the embryo transfer trans-vaginally using ultrasound guidance. We also provide medication to support the pregnancy after the embryo transfer.

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Defence Colony?

items.t: High Age and Low Ovarian Reserve
items.d: Using DuoStim, we can obtain multiple blastocysts with a personalised dose. We can bank blastocysts for the future if you get fewer eggs or poor quality.
We do an extensive work-up of your blastocyst, uterus and timing after unsuccessful IVF cycles. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).

We use low-dose stimulation to obtain eggs without increasing your hormone levels, and down-regulation before frozen embryo transfers. See [Endometriosis & Adenomyosis](/endometriosis-fertility-treatment/).
This helps identify whether your blastocysts are chromosomally normal. We suggest it if you have failed a few IVF cycles or are on the higher side of age.
Egg freezing is possible if you want to postpone pregnancy or have an illness that requires chemotherapy. See [Oncofertility](/oncofertility-cancer-fertility-preservation/).

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: AMH and Day 2/Day 3 scan to know ovarian reserve.
Semen test for the husband with computer-assisted semen analysis and DNA fragmentation.
Ultrasound scan or SIS to rule out polyps and fibroids inside the uterus. Hysteroscopy is performed if needed.
Blood work-up for diabetes and thyroid to see if they are in control.
Basal hormonal test on Day 2 of your cycle: FSH, LH, Estradiol.
HIV 1 & 2, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and VDRL tests for both partners are mandatory under the ART Act.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

steps.t: Meet us to know what treatment protocol you can go with
sub: By knowing your current reports, we decide which protocol is best for you
Injections run from Day 2 to Day 11 depending on your case. Visit us every 2–3 days for scans and blood work
You will be under mild sedation while your doctor aspirates your follicles, and your partner provides a sperm sample
The lab staff fertilise your eggs by ICSI. Eggs are kept in the incubator for 5 days
We pick a good quality blastocyst and transfer it into your uterus under ultrasound. Hormones are given to support your pregnancy

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Check ovarian reserve: AMH blood test and scan to see the number of eggs. Day 2/3 ultrasound to check antral follicle count.
Semen analysis: the male partner's semen is checked by CASA. Semen DNA fragmentation may be needed.
Imaging of the uterus: 3D ultrasound or SIS may be needed. Sometimes a diagnostic HSG or hysteroscopy can be useful.
Bloods for thyroid and diabetes: serum TSH, prolactin and HbA1c. Scan and Day 2 bloods to check FSH, LH and estradiol levels.
Mandatory tests as per ART Act before starting any procedure: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL, for both female and male partners.

sections.eyebrow: What We Do to Treat You

sub: Review previous reports and plan the protocol based on ovarian reserve and the male partner's semen analysis.

On the final day of stimulation we aspirate your follicles and do lab work on your partner's sample.
Micropipette injection of sperm into your eggs (ICSI); embryos grow in the incubator until the blastocyst stage (Day 5).
Transfer of your best blastocyst under ultrasound guidance. You start luteal support medicines and wait for pregnancy.

items.d: Our protocol with DuoStim and freezing embryos can be useful. As women age they tend to lose the quantity and quality of their eggs.

sections.eyebrow: How Do We Test If You Are Infertile?
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Check your ovarian reserve: test for AMH level in blood and antral follicle count on a Day 2/3 ultrasound.
Semen analysis by computer tells us your sperm count, motility and shape. We can also check DNA fragmentation if required.
A 3D ultrasound or SIS can be used to rule out any uterine pathology. Hysteroscopy can be done if needed.
Check your thyroid (TSH), prolactin and sugar levels (HbA1c) along with a Day 2 hormone profile.
The ART Act states that everyone undergoing IVF must be screened for HIV 1 & 2, HBsAg, Anti-HCV and VDRL, both female and male.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

items.d: At our clinic we use different protocols to increase egg retrieval numbers. One of them is DuoStim, which gives you double the eggs of a normal IVF protocol. If you have low AMH you can also store your embryos.
If you have had unsuccessful IVF cycles, you should know what leads to implantation failure. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Patients with endometriosis have higher success rates when using a modified protocol. See [Endometriosis & Adenomyosis](/endometriosis-fertility-treatment/).
When your age is more than 35 years or you have a history of recurrent pregnancy loss, you should know what PGT-A is and how it can help you achieve a healthy pregnancy.
If you wish to postpone your pregnancy, you can freeze your eggs or embryos for the future. See [Pregnancy After Cancer](/oncofertility-cancer-fertility-preservation/).

sections.eyebrow: What Tests Do I Need Before Treatment
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Blood workup to check your ovarian reserve: AMH. A scan on Day 2/3 to see how many follicles you have (AFC).
Your husband needs to send a semen sample for analysis of count and DNA fragmentation index.
Ultrasound / SIS (if any abnormality) and hysteroscopy if required, to look for the cause of infertility and any correction needed in your uterus.
Thyroid profile (TSH), prolactin level, HbA1c and hormone profile on Day 2: FSH, LH and estradiol.
Tests mandated by the ART Act: blood test for infections like HIV 1 & 2, hepatitis B & C and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Based on the data we already have about you, Dr Mona Dahiya will evaluate your case.
Your ovaries will be given drugs that induce you to make more eggs/follicles. This is monitored with ultrasounds and blood work.

When the follicles are at optimum size you will be taken to the OT and your eggs will be picked using ultrasound. This is a painless procedure done under light anaesthesia. Semen is collected at the same time.
We use your husband's sperm to inject into the mature eggs and cultivate them until the Day 5 blastocyst stage.
A healthy blastocyst is transferred into your uterus using TVUS. You will be prescribed medicines after transfer.

items.t: Reduced Egg Count and Higher Age Group (Above 35 Years)

items.t: Failure of Embryo Transfer (Recurrent Implantation Failure)
items.d: We diagnose why embryo transfer failed using advanced technology and methods, evaluating embryo, uterine and other factors to find the cause of implantation failure. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).

items.t: IVF in Case of Endometriosis and Adenomyosis
items.d: Different ovarian stimulation protocols are followed so as not to deplete the ovaries of eggs. We also perform down regulation before embryo transfer. See [Endometriosis & Adenomyosis](/endometriosis-fertility-treatment/).
Helpful in identifying blastocysts that are free from chromosome defects. Only if the patient is more than 35 years of age or in cases of previous miscarriages. Not recommended for all patients.
If you wish to freeze your eggs or embryos, cryopreservation is the answer. Store embryos until you are ready to conceive. See [Oncofertility](/oncofertility-cancer-fertility-preservation/).

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Evaluate ovarian reserve: serum AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone) level and Day 2/3 follicular count (by USG transvaginal scanning).
Male factor infertility: semen analysis is done (CASA). In some cases sperm DNA fragmentation can also be tested.
Shape of uterus: by ultrasound or SIS and, if indicated, by hysteroscopy.
Serum levels: Day 2 hormones FSH, LH, estrogen should be checked. Thyroid profile (TSH), serum prolactin level and fasting blood sugar/HbA1c should also be normal before starting IVF.
Mandatory blood work as per ART Act: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL (both partners need to undergo screening).

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: History from the patient and past treatment, if any, will be noted. Basic investigations to check ovarian reserve and male factor will be done. Then we will decide the IVF protocol.
Hormonal injections are prescribed and you need to visit our centre for checking growth of follicles (by scan) and hormone levels in blood.
Eggs are retrieved under light sedation and sperm is collected from the partner and prepared in our laboratory.
Eggs and sperm are mixed together to get embryos in a process called fertilisation. Embryos are then grown in incubators for 5 days.
We do ultrasound-guided embryo transfer on Day 5, after the embryo reaches the blastocyst stage. Medications are also given after transfer to support the lining.

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Janakpuri?

items.d: Want to know why you failed in your previous IVF cycles? See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Find out what caused you to miscarry. It could be due to genetics, uterine abnormality, hormones or a male factor, i.e. high DFI. See [Sperm DNA Fragmentation](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/).
Want to test your embryos for chromosomal defects? Do PGT-A if needed.
You can bank your good embryos for future pregnancies or create siblings for your children. See [Embryo Freezing & Banking](/embryo-cryopreservation/).
If you have polyps, septum or any other pathology in your uterus, it can be corrected through hysteroscopy prior to your embryo transfer.

sections.eyebrow: Tests You Will Need to Get Done Before Starting Your Treatment
sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
points: Ovarian reserve testing: blood work to check your AMH level and ultrasound scanning to count your number of follicles on Day 2/3 of the cycle.
Semen testing for the male partner. We can also do a DNA fragmentation test if necessary.
Ultrasound scan to look at your uterine cavity. A 3D USG or SIS can be performed to look at the cavity, and hysteroscopy if needed.
Basic blood tests like thyroid profile (TSH & prolactin levels) and diabetes profile (HbA1c level) along with hormones (Day 2/3 FSH, LH & estradiol).
Blood tests to screen for contagious diseases like Hep B, Hep C, HIV & VDRL for both partners as mandated by the ART Act.

sections.eyebrow: What We Will Do When You Start Your Cycle
sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: We will look at your reports and decide the best drug protocol for your ovarian reserve.

Your IVF cycle will start with drugs on Day 2/3 of the cycle. We use injections known as gonadotropins. Your follicles will be scanned and monitored with blood work on every alternate day. This will go on for about 8–10 days.
When your follicles are matured, we will collect your eggs. This is a simple procedure performed with ultrasound guidance under light sedation. Your spouse's sperm sample will also be collected.
Our lab team will do ICSI on your eggs, which is a form of fertilisation. We will incubate these embryos till they reach Day 5. Embryos are called blastocysts at Day 5.

Depending upon the number of embryos and their quality, you will have your transfer either fresh or frozen. Embryo transfer is done with ultrasound guidance on a suitable endometrium. Progesterone is started post transfer.

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Paschim Vihar?

items.d: A second opinion that reviews stimulation, embryos, transfer and uterus. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Investigation of genetic, uterine, hormonal and sperm factors, including [Sperm DNA Fragmentation](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/) testing.
Chromosomal testing of blastocysts when age or repeated loss makes it worthwhile.
Freezing good embryos for future transfers or a sibling through [Embryo Freezing & Banking](/embryo-cryopreservation/).
Polyps, septum or adhesions corrected by hysteroscopy before the next transfer.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: These tests confirm the cause and shape your plan. Not every couple needs every test.
points: Ovarian reserve testing: serum AMH and a Day 2/3 transvaginal scan for antral follicle count (AFC).
Semen assessment: computer-assisted semen analysis (CASA) with DNA fragmentation testing when indicated.
Uterine cavity screening: 3D sonography or saline infusion sonography, with hysteroscopy when needed.
Hormone and metabolic profile: TSH, prolactin, HbA1c and baseline Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
ART Act serology for both partners: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Review of previous reports, ovarian reserve and semen results to design your own protocol
Tailored gonadotropin doses with ultrasound follicle tracking and hormone checks
A short, ultrasound-guided procedure under light sedation, with sperm prepared in the lab at the same time
Embryos grown to the Day 5 blastocyst stage in benchtop incubators
Ultrasound-guided transfer of a selected blastocyst into a well-prepared lining, followed by luteal support

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Tagore Garden?

items.d: A second opinion that reviews stimulation, embryos, transfer and uterus. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Investigation of genetic, uterine, hormonal and sperm factors, including [Sperm DNA Fragmentation](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/) testing.
Chromosomal testing of blastocysts when age or repeated loss makes it worthwhile.
Freezing good embryos for future transfers or a sibling through [Embryo Freezing & Banking](/embryo-cryopreservation/).
Polyps, septum or adhesions corrected by hysteroscopy before the next transfer.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: These tests confirm the cause and shape your plan. Not every couple needs every test.
points: Ovarian reserve testing: serum AMH and a Day 2/3 transvaginal scan for antral follicle count (AFC).
Semen assessment: computer-assisted semen analysis (CASA) with DNA fragmentation testing when indicated.
Uterine cavity screening: 3D sonography or saline infusion sonography, with hysteroscopy when needed.
Hormone and metabolic profile: TSH, prolactin, HbA1c and baseline Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
ART Act serology for both partners: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Review of previous reports, ovarian reserve and semen results to design your own protocol
Tailored gonadotropin doses with ultrasound follicle tracking and hormone checks
A short, ultrasound-guided procedure under light sedation, with sperm prepared in the lab at the same time
Embryos grown to the Day 5 blastocyst stage in benchtop incubators
Ultrasound-guided transfer of a selected blastocyst into a well-prepared lining, followed by luteal support

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Jhandewalan?

items.d: A second opinion that reviews stimulation, embryos, transfer and uterus. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Investigation of genetic, uterine, hormonal and sperm factors, including [Sperm DNA Fragmentation](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/) testing.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: These tests confirm the cause and shape your plan. Not every couple needs every test.
points: Ovarian reserve testing: serum AMH and a Day 2/3 transvaginal scan for antral follicle count (AFC).

Uterine cavity screening: 3D sonography or saline infusion sonography, with hysteroscopy when needed.
Hormone and metabolic profile: TSH, prolactin, HbA1c and baseline Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
ART Act serology for both partners: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

Embryos grown to the Day 5 blastocyst stage in benchtop incubators
Ultrasound-guided transfer of a selected blastocyst into a well-prepared lining, followed by luteal support

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Paharganj?

items.d: A second opinion that reviews stimulation, embryos, transfer and uterus. See [Recurrent Implantation Failure (RIF)](/recurrent-implantation-failure-rif/).
Investigation of genetic, uterine, hormonal and sperm factors, including [Sperm DNA Fragmentation](/sperm-dna-fragmentation-test/) testing.
Chromosomal testing of blastocysts when age or repeated loss makes it worthwhile.
Freezing good embryos for future transfers or a sibling through [Embryo Freezing & Banking](/embryo-cryopreservation/).
Polyps, septum or adhesions corrected by hysteroscopy before the next transfer.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: These tests confirm the cause and shape your plan. Not every couple needs every test.
points: Ovarian reserve testing: serum AMH and a Day 2/3 transvaginal scan for antral follicle count (AFC).
Semen assessment: computer-assisted semen analysis (CASA) with DNA fragmentation testing when indicated.
Uterine cavity screening: 3D sonography or saline infusion sonography, with hysteroscopy when needed.
Hormone and metabolic profile: TSH, prolactin, HbA1c and baseline Day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
ART Act serology for both partners: HIV I & II, HBsAg, anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Review of previous reports, ovarian reserve and semen results to design your own protocol
Tailored gonadotropin doses with ultrasound follicle tracking and hormone checks
A short, ultrasound-guided procedure under light sedation, with sperm prepared in the lab at the same time
Embryos grown to the Day 5 blastocyst stage in benchtop incubators
Ultrasound-guided transfer of a selected blastocyst into a well-prepared lining, followed by luteal support

sections.h2: Why Paharganj Residents Consult Dr. Mona Dahiya

items.d: Our Lajpat Nagar, South Delhi clinic is about 10 km away (20–30 min by road).
MBBS (Gold Medalist, Lady Hardinge Medical College), MD (Gold Medalist, Maulana Azad Medical College), DNB, and a Fellowship in IVF from Singapore General Hospital.
Dr. Mona Dahiya plans your protocol, reviews your scans and performs the embryo transfer herself.

sections.h2: Indications: Who Needs Advanced Fertility Care in Sector 49?

items.d: We use individual protocol of stimulation for woman with less than 1.1 ng/ml AMH by using DuoStim technique along with micro dose flare.
In case of severe male factor such as low sperm count (oligospermia) with OATS or increased sperm DFI (>25%) and azoospermia (PESA/TESA/micro TESE).
If you have undergone unsuccessful IVF cycle in another hospital, 3D SIS and hysteroscopy will be performed. ERA can be performed in case of repeated failure.
We recommend doing embryo cryopreservation or banking. After 2 to 3 months of depo inj. do frozen embryo transfer.
Antagonist protocol is used and we trigger with agonist giving you no chance of OHSS.

sections.h2: Diagnostic Checklist: Pre-IVF Evaluation
paras: Tests required prior to starting IVF.
points: Check ovarian reserve: AMH levels and USG done on day 2 or 3 for good AFC.
Male workup: Semen analysis with CASA and halo sperm test should be done after 2 to 3 days abstinence.
Saline sonography: Performed to assess uterus receptivity. Biopsy of endometrium can be taken to check CD138.
Blood work: Thyroid profile and fasting insulin/HbA1C. Hormonal assessment of day 2 FSH, LH and estradiol.
Serology test for ART: Partner should do their HIV 1/2, HBsAg, Anti-HCV and VDRL.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Clinical Treatment Protocol

sub: Your medical record will be evaluated. USG is done for follicle size and your past investigation will be reviewed.

steps.t: Protocol of Stim Will Run from Day 2 to Day 11 of Cycle
sub: From day 2 you will be started on injection given daily and monitored by USG and anti-Mullerian hormone.

steps.t: Pick Up of Eggs and Semen Analysis
sub: Procedure is carried out under local anaesthesia which takes approximately 15 minutes, USG guided. Sperm is processed in laminar flow.

steps.t: On Day 1 ICSI and 5th Day Embryo
sub: After ICSI is performed we will monitor embryo till day 5 to 6 which is called blastocyst.
Fresh or frozen embryo will be transferred under USG guidance using soft catheter.

sections.h2: Why Sector 49 Residents Consult Dr Mona Dahiya

items.d: With 25+ years of experience, she has completed her MBBS and MD as a gold medallist from Delhi, followed by DNB and fellowship from Singapore General Hospital.
She will plan your protocol and sit with you during scans. She will also perform your embryo transfer.
Clean room with laser assisted hatching is available at our clinic. Vitrify your embryo in closed system.

sections.h2: Illustrative Patient Scenario
sections.cap: Disclaimer: this case is very common and happens in the majority of our patients. Outcomes may vary.
sections.text: Lady of 29 years with PCOS who comes from Sector 49. She was told by another doctor to not proceed for IUI because of growth of follicles. She underwent one cycle of ICSI with antagonist and trigger with agonist. We froze her embryo and after a month performed FET resulting in singleton baby.
